headline: Easy-run HR keeps drifting down as the four-week block closes with volume up and strength doubled — base is consolidating well.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The aerobic-efficiency signal you've been building is still the clearest thing in the data: comparable-effort easy runs are sitting at a lower heart rate than the prior period, which is exactly what you want to see with volume up by half over the previous block. That combination — more kilometres carried at a lower cost — is consolidation, not fatigue.

Strength has genuinely stepped up too, roughly doubling in frequency, and it's holding alongside the running rather than being crowded out. With St. Olavsleden a few weeks out, this looks like a base that's ready and now settling. The strain:tolerance ratio still reads productive, so nothing here argues for backing off; today's picture is a durable block finishing in good order.

Sleep is worth a passing note only — it's been swinging hard between very short and very long nights, but that stream isn't validated enough to shift anything, and the strain ratio isn't corroborating any concern.
watch_items: Whether the short/long sleep swings settle into a steadier pattern or begin clustering short as the event approaches.
Whether pack-loaded running enters the schedule, since the general base looks ready but the specific weighted demand still isn't trained.
Whether ascent per run starts trending toward sustained climbing to match the mountain crossing, rather than the rolling profiles logged so far.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 190 km vs 126 km prior block (+51%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 145 bpm vs 153 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 8 runs)
▬ Strain:tolerance ratio 1.08 (PRODUCTIVE) (strain 91, tolerance 85); sleep averaging 7h36m over the same period
